REASONING: La evidencia ahora es muy clara: el proceso es esencialmente Poisson en todos los puntos vistos, pero la media tiene un cambio brusco de pendiente al pasar 1.2. El ajuste lineal por tramos captura bien 1.28 y 1.4, aunque subestima algo 1.1; como la evaluación probablemente use varios speeds, conviene refinar la forma bajo 1.2 y mantener el tramo alto fuerte. El siguiente paso es comparar varias parametrizaciones de la media usando todos los puntos observados — por ejemplo, lineal por tramos vs cuadrática abajo + lineal arriba — y elegir una antes del segundo piloto.
```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

pts = pd.DataFrame({
    "speed": [0.8, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.28, 1.4],
    "mean":  [5.1875, 6.54625, 7.3, 7.4625, 11.1125, 19.383333333333333],
})
x = pts["speed"].to_numpy()
y = pts["mean"].to_numpy()

# Model A: piecewise linear with knot at 1.2
XA = np.column_stack([np.ones_like(x), x - 1.0, np.maximum(0, x - 1.2)])
coefA, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(XA, y, rcond=None)
predA = XA @ coefA

# Model B: quadratic below/near 1.2 plus post-1.2 slope change
XB = np.column_stack([np.ones_like(x), x - 1.0, (x - 1.0)**2, np.maximum(0, x - 1.2)])
coefB, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(XB, y, rcond=None)
predB = XB @ coefB

# Model C: exponential below 1.2, then extra linear term above 1.2 on mean scale
# Fit by least squares over transformed features [exp basis approximated by log-linear for low region] is awkward;
# instead compare a simple piecewise log-mean model by linear regression on log(y).
XC = np.column_stack([np.ones_like(x), x - 1.0, np.maximum(0, x - 1.2)])
coefC, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(XC, np.log(y), rcond=None)
predC = np.exp(XC @ coefC)

def sse(pred): return float(np.sum((y - pred)**2))

print("fit SSEs:", {
    "A_piecewise_linear_mean": sse(predA),
    "B_quadratic_below_plus_jump_slope": sse(predB),
    "C_piecewise_loglinear_mean": sse(predC),
})
out = pts.copy()
```

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

pts = pd.DataFrame({
    "speed": [0.8, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.28, 1.4],
    "mean":  [5.1875, 6.54625, 7.3, 7.4625, 11.1125, 19.383333333333333],
})
x = pts["speed"].to_numpy()
y = pts["mean"].to_numpy()

# Model A: piecewise linear with knot at 1.2
XA = np.column_stack([np.ones_like(x), x - 1.0, np.maximum(0, x - 1.2)])
coefA, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(XA, y, rcond=None)
predA = XA @ coefA

# Model B: quadratic below/near 1.2 plus post-1.2 slope change
XB = np.column_stack([np.ones_like(x), x - 1.0, (x - 1.0)**2, np.maximum(0, x - 1.2)])
coefB, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(XB, y, rcond=None)
predB = XB @ coefB

# Model C: exponential below 1.2, then extra linear term above 1.2 on mean scale
# Fit by least squares over transformed features [exp basis approximated by log-linear for low region] is awkward;
# instead compare a simple piecewise log-mean model by linear regression on log(y).
XC = np.column_stack([np.ones_like(x), x - 1.0, np.maximum(0, x - 1.2)])
coefC, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(XC, np.log(y), rcond=None)
predC = np.exp(XC @ coefC)

def sse(pred): return float(np.sum((y - pred)**2))

print("fit SSEs:", {
    "A_piecewise_linear_mean": sse(predA),
    "B_quadratic_below_plus_jump_slope": sse(predB),
    "C_piecewise_loglinear_mean": sse(predC),
})
out = pts.copy()
out["pred_A"] = predA
out["pred_B"] = predB
out["pred_C"] = predC
print(out)

# store best candidate coefficients for later if desired
best = min(
    [("A", sse(predA), coefA), ("B", sse(predB), coefB), ("C", sse(predC), coefC)],
    key=lambda t: t[1]
)
print("best:", best[0], "coef:", best[2].tolist())
